    • Negative Binomial and Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial Regression from Scratch: the nbzinbCirkovic Package

nbzinbCirkovic

Negative binomial (NB) and zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) regression, with the estimation implemented from scratch:

  • nbreg() fits NB2 regression by iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) for the coefficients, alternated with Newton–Raphson updates of log(θ).
  • zinbreg() fits ZINB regression by an EM algorithm whose M-steps are IRLS fits (a weighted logistic regression for the zero part and a weighted NB regression for the count part). Standard errors come from an analytic Hessian of the observed-data log-likelihood.

No general-purpose numerical maximizer is used. The results agree with MASS::glm.nb() and pscl::zeroinfl(); see the benchmark in the report.

STA 651 final project (Fall 2026), David Cirkovic.

  • Website: https://cirkovicdavid.github.io/nbzinbCirkovic/ (function reference and the project report)
  • Report (PDF): report/report.pdf

Installation 

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("cirkovicdavid/nbzinbCirkovic")

Since devtools 2.5.0, install_github() needs the remotes package; if the command above reports that “remotes” is required, run install.packages("remotes") first, or use either of

remotes::install_github("cirkovicdavid/nbzinbCirkovic")
pak::pak("cirkovicdavid/nbzinbCirkovic")

Usage 

library(nbzinbCirkovic)
data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")

# Negative binomial regression
fit_nb <- nbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment, data = bioChemists)
summary(fit_nb)
#> Coefficients (negative binomial with log link):
#>              Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)
#> (Intercept)  0.256144   0.137348   1.865 0.062191 .
#> femWomen    -0.216418   0.072636  -2.979 0.002887 **
#> marMarried   0.150489   0.082097   1.833 0.066791 .
#> kid5        -0.176415   0.052813  -3.340 0.000837 ***
#> phd          0.015271   0.035873   0.426 0.670326
#> ment         0.029082   0.003214   9.048  < 2e-16 ***
#>
#> Theta: 2.264   Std. Error: 0.2712
#> Log-likelihood: -1560.96 on 7 df   AIC: 3135.92

# Zero-inflated NB: count covariates | zero-inflation covariates
fit_zinb <- zinbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment | ment,
                    data = bioChemists)
summary(fit_zinb)

# Standard methods work for both classes
AIC(fit_nb, fit_zinb)
predict(fit_zinb, newdata = bioChemists[1:3, ], type = "zero")  # P(structural zero)
residuals(fit_nb, type = "pearson")

Use nbreg_control(trace = TRUE) or zinbreg_control(trace = TRUE) to print the log-likelihood at every iteration; for zinbreg() it never decreases, as the EM algorithm guarantees.
